6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.EntryIdealStratum
7	
8	/-!
9	# Ring-level upper semicontinuity of the fibre rank
10	
11	**Campaign milestone B5, algebraic core.**  For a finitely presented module
12	`M` over a commutative ring `R`, the sublevel locus of the fibre dimension
13	
14	```
15	{p : PrimeSpectrum R | p.asIdeal.fiberRank M ≤ e}
16	```
17	
18	is **open**, with no flatness, noetherian or finiteness hypothesis on `R`.
19	
20	## Why this file exists beside `PointRankSemicontinuity.lean`
21	
22	`Picard/PointRankSemicontinuity.lean` proves the *geometric* statement
23	`Scheme.Modules.isOpen_pointRank_le` — openness of `{s : S | pointRank S F s ≤ e}`
24	for a quasi-coherent `F` on a locally noetherian scheme `S`.  That is the same
25	mathematics one level up, and it is *not* the statement below: `pointRank`
26	is defined through a `choose`n affine chart and its `fiberRank` is taken at a
27	prime of `Γ(S, V)` for that chart, whereas this file's `fiberRank` is taken at a
28	prime of `R` itself with the `R`-module structure.  Measured in the earlier
29	round: the two are not the same term and `rfl` between them fails
30	(recorded as obligation (c) at `Picard/FiberH0Comparison.lean`:66-82).
31	
32	Working at the ring level has three concrete consequences:
33	
34	* **`IsLocallyNoetherian` disappears.**  The geometric proof runs through
35	  `Scheme.Modules.chartLocus`, whose construction needs the noetherian
36	  hypothesis; the affine argument below needs only `Module.FinitePresentation`.
37	* **No quasi-coherence side condition**, since there is no sheaf.
38	* It is the form the **two-term complex** consumers want: the fibres of a
39	  Čech complex's terms are modules over the base ring, not sheaves on it.
40	
41	## The proof
42	
43	The Nakayama prolongation `Module.FinitePresentation.exists_matrixPresentation_of_isLocalizedModule`
44	(`Picard/EntryIdeal.lean`, Nitsure §4) gives, for each prime `p`, an element
45	`g ∉ p` such that `M` localized away from `g` admits a matrix presentation with
46	exactly `p.fiberRank M` generators.  On the basic open `D(g)`:
47	
48	* every prime `q ∈ D(g)` lifts to a prime `Q` of `R[1/g]`
49	  (`PrimeSpectrum.localization_away_comap_range`);
50	* `Ideal.fiberRank_of_isLocalizedModule` identifies `M`'s fibre rank at `q`
51	  with the localized module's fibre rank at `Q`;
52	* `Module.MatrixPresentation.fiberRank_le` bounds the latter by the generator
53	  count `p.fiberRank M ≤ e`.
54	
55	So `D(g)` is an open neighbourhood of `p` inside the sublevel locus.  Every
56	ingredient was already in the tree; what was missing is that the prolongation's
57	generator count *is* the bound the sublevel set asks for.
58	
59	## References
60	
61	Nitsure, *Construction of Hilbert and Quot schemes*, §4 (the local
62	`e`-generator presentation).  Hartshorne III 12.8; Mumford, *Abelian
63	Varieties*, II §5.  Stacks 00NX.
64	-/
65	
66	set_option autoImplicit false
67	
68	universe u
69	
70	open Module
71	
72	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {M : Type u} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
73	
74	namespace Ideal
75	
76	/-- **Upper semicontinuity of the fibre rank, ring level.**
77	
78	For `M` finitely presented over `R`, the set of primes at which the fibre
79	`κ(p) ⊗_R M` has dimension at most `e` is open in `Spec R`.  No flatness, and
80	no noetherian hypothesis on `R`.
81	
82	Contrast `Module.isLocallyConstant_rankAtStalk`, which needs `M` *flat* and
83	concludes the strictly stronger local constancy; without flatness the rank
84	genuinely jumps and only this sublevel direction survives. -/
85	theorem isOpen_fiberRank_le [Module.FinitePresentation R M] (e : ℕ) :
86	    IsOpen {p : PrimeSpectrum R | p.asIdeal.fiberRank M ≤ e} := by
87	  rw [isOpen_iff_forall_mem_open]
88	  intro p hp
89	  -- Nakayama prolongation at `p`: a `p.fiberRank M`-generator presentation
90	  -- survives on a basic open `D(g)` around `p`.
91	  obtain ⟨g, hg, hpres⟩ :=
92	    Module.FinitePresentation.exists_matrixPresentation_of_isLocalizedModule.{u, u, u, u}
93	      (R := R) (M := M) p.asIdeal
94	  obtain ⟨mm, ⟨P⟩⟩ := hpres (Localization.Away g)
95	    (LocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers g) M)
96	    (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap (Submonoid.powers g) M)
97	  refine ⟨(PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen g : Set (PrimeSpectrum R)), ?_,
98	    (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen g).isOpen, hg⟩
99	  intro q hq
100	  -- `q` avoids `g`, hence lifts to a prime `Q` of `R[1/g]`.
101	  have hrange : q ∈ Set.range (PrimeSpectrum.comap
102	      (algebraMap R (Localization.Away g))) := by
103	    rw [PrimeSpectrum.localization_away_comap_range (Localization.Away g) g]
104	    exact hq
105	  obtain ⟨Q, hQ⟩ := hrange
106	  have hloc := Ideal.fiberRank_of_isLocalizedModule (R := R) (M := M)
107	    (Submonoid.powers g) (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap (Submonoid.powers g) M) Q.asIdeal
108	  have hcomap : Q.asIdeal.comap (algebraMap R (Localization.Away g)) = q.asIdeal := by
109	    rw [← hQ]; rfl
110	  change q.asIdeal.fiberRank M ≤ e
111	  calc q.asIdeal.fiberRank M
112	      = (Q.asIdeal.comap (algebraMap R (Localization.Away g))).fiberRank M :=
113	        Ideal.fiberRank_congr_ideal hcomap.symm
114	    _ = Q.asIdeal.fiberRank (LocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers g) M) := hloc.symm
115	    _ ≤ p.asIdeal.fiberRank M := Module.MatrixPresentation.fiberRank_le P Q.asIdeal
116	    _ ≤ e := hp
117	
118	/-- **Ring level, closed form**: the superlevel locus of the fibre rank is
119	closed.  The set-theoretic complement of `isOpen_fiberRank_le`; the `ℕ`-valued
120	rank makes `e + 1 ≤ r` and `¬ (r ≤ e)` the same condition. -/
121	theorem isClosed_le_fiberRank [Module.FinitePresentation R M] (e : ℕ) :
122	    IsClosed {p : PrimeSpectrum R | e + 1 ≤ p.asIdeal.fiberRank M} := by
123	  have hcompl : {p : PrimeSpectrum R | e + 1 ≤ p.asIdeal.fiberRank M}
124	      = {p : PrimeSpectrum R | p.asIdeal.fiberRank M ≤ e}ᶜ := by
125	    ext p
126	    simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq, Set.mem_compl_iff, not_le]
127	    omega
128	  rw [hcompl]
129	  exact (isOpen_fiberRank_le e).isClosed_compl
130	
131	end Ideal

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.FiberRankSemicontinuity
7	
8	/-!
9	# B5's engine: upper semicontinuity of `dim H⁰` for a two-term complex
10	
11	**Campaign milestone B5, the Mumford minors argument, done through cokernels.**
12	
13	For a two-term complex `k : K → Aⁿ` with `K` finitely presented and
14	projective — the shape `TwoTermFiniteReplacement` produces
15	(`Picard/TwoTermFiniteFree.lean`:507, fields `K0`, `n`, `projective_K0`) —
16	the locus
17	
18	```
19	{t : Spec A | dim_κ(t) ker (k ⊗ κ(t)) ≤ e}
20	```
21	
22	is **open**.  That is upper semicontinuity of the fibrewise `H⁰` of the
23	complex, which is what B5 asks for once `H⁰` is presented as a kernel.
24	
25	## Why this route works where the prescribed one cannot
26	
27	`Picard/SemicontinuityH0.lean`:55-57 prescribes discharging the gate through
28	the *rank bridge* `rank_pushforward_eq_fiberH0`.  Measured in the previous
29	round and filed as I-0884: that bridge carries `hproj`, which its own file
30	proves load-bearing by counterexample, and finite projectivity forces the rank
31	**locally constant** — strictly stronger than the semicontinuity wanted.  The
32	prescription inverts the difficulty.
33	
34	The route below never touches that bridge.  It puts the projectivity where
35	projectivity is *true and harmless* — on `K`, the replacement's degree-0 term,
36	which is projective by construction — and gets the jumping from the **cokernel**,
37	which is only finitely presented and whose fibre rank genuinely jumps:
38	
39	```
40	dim ker (k ⊗ κ)  +  n  =  dim (κ ⊗ K)  +  dim coker (k ⊗ κ)        (rank-nullity)
41	                          ─────────────    ────────────────────
42	                          locally CONSTANT   upper semicontinuous
43	                          (K proj. + flat)   (Ideal.isOpen_fiberRank_le)
44	```
45	
46	Near a point `t₀` the first summand is a constant `r`, so on that neighbourhood
47	
48	```
49	{dim ker ≤ e}  =  {fiberRank K = r}  ∩  {fiberRank (coker k) ≤ e + n − r},
50	```
51	
52	an intersection of two opens.  The jumping of `dim ker` is exactly the jumping
53	of `dim coker`, transported by an identity that costs nothing.
54	
55	## The junk-value hazard is closed structurally, not assumed
56	
57	`Picard/FiberH0Comparison.lean`:38-55 records obligation (b): `Module.finrank`
58	returns `0` in the infinite-dimensional case, on both sides, so a rank identity
59	can hold vacuously as `0 = 0`.  Here that cannot happen, and **no hypothesis is
60	needed to rule it out**: `κ(t) ⊗_A K` is finite-dimensional because `K` is
61	`Module.Finite` (implied by `Module.FinitePresentation`), and `κ(t) ⊗_A Aⁿ` is
62	`n`-dimensional outright.  Both are automatic instances — `FiniteDimensional`
63	is synthesised, not supplied.  So every `finrank` below is a genuine dimension.
64	
65	## What this does and does not discharge
66	
67	**Discharges**, sorry-free: the semicontinuity statement for any two-term
68	complex of the replacement's shape, over any commutative ring, with no
69	noetherian hypothesis and no `h¹`-vanishing.  Obligation (b) of the three
70	recorded at `Picard/FiberH0Comparison.lean`:79-82 is closed outright — not
71	weakened, not moved: finite-dimensionality is now a consequence rather than an
72	antecedent.
73	
74	**Does not discharge**: `Scheme.HasH0Semicontinuity`
75	(`Picard/SemicontinuityH0.lean`:93) is still **open**, and this file does not
76	instantiate it.  Two obligations stand between the two statements, and they are
77	the (a) and (c) of that list:
78	
79	* (a) the curve's Čech complex must be *replaced* by one of this shape.
80	  `exists_twoTermFiniteReplacement` (`Picard/TwoTermFiniteFree.lean`:545) does
81	  produce `K0` projective and `K¹ = Aⁿ` free, so the shape matches — but it
82	  needs `Module.Flat` on both terms of the original and finite generation of
83	  `H⁰`/`H¹`, and its `h0_bijective` field compares the replacement's `H⁰` with
84	  the original's, which is a further identification not made here;
85	* (c) the carrier bridge: `κ(t)`-dimension of a *kernel over `A`* against
86	  `Scheme.Hom.fiberH0`, the dimension of `Γ(C_t, L_t)`.  Steps 4-6 of
87	  `fiberRank_gammaTop_eq_fiberH0` (`Picard/FiberH0Comparison.lean`) are
88	  hypothesis-free and do exactly this transport for the Čech difference map,
89	  so the bridge is a composition rather than a new theorem — but it has not
90	  been composed, and until it is, no statement here is about a curve.
91	
92	So: an implication proved, with (a) and (c) named and open.  Nothing below
93	should be read as "B5 is closed".
94	
95	## References
96	
97	Mumford, *Abelian Varieties*, II §5 Lemma 1 (the two-term finite replacement
98	and its minors); EGA III 6.10.5; Hartshorne III 12.8; Stacks 00NX, 02KG.
99	-/
100	
101	set_option autoImplicit false
102	
103	universe u
104	
105	open Module TensorProduct
106	
107	variable {A : Type u} [CommRing A] {K : Type u} [AddCommGroup K] [Module A K]
108	
109	namespace AlgebraicJacobian
110	
111	namespace TwoTerm
112	
113	/-- **Base change commutes with cokernels**, in the fibre-rank form B5 uses:
114	the fibre rank of `coker k` at `t` is the `κ(t)`-dimension of the cokernel of
115	the base-changed map.
116	
117	Right-exactness of `κ(t) ⊗_A -`, packaged as a `finrank` identity.  (The
118	sibling project carries the same equivalence as
119	`LinearMap.quotRangeBaseChangeEquiv`; it is re-derived here rather than
120	imported, since AJC does not depend on that project.) -/
121	theorem fiberRank_quotRange_eq_finrank_quot_baseChange {N : Type u} [AddCommGroup N]
122	    [Module A N] (k : K →ₗ[A] N) (t : PrimeSpectrum A) :
123	    t.asIdeal.fiberRank (N ⧸ LinearMap.range k)
124	      = Module.finrank t.asIdeal.ResidueField
125	          ((t.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[A] N) ⧸
126	            LinearMap.range (k.baseChange t.asIdeal.ResidueField)) := by
127	  have hker : LinearMap.ker ((LinearMap.range k).mkQ.baseChange t.asIdeal.ResidueField)
128	      = LinearMap.range (k.baseChange t.asIdeal.ResidueField) := by
129	    apply LinearMap.exact_iff.mp
130	    rw [LinearMap.baseChange_eq_ltensor, LinearMap.baseChange_eq_ltensor]
131	    exact lTensor_exact _ (LinearMap.exact_map_mkQ_range k) (Submodule.mkQ_surjective _)
132	  have hsurj : Function.Surjective
133	      ((LinearMap.range k).mkQ.baseChange t.asIdeal.ResidueField) := by
134	    rw [LinearMap.baseChange_eq_ltensor]
135	    exact LinearMap.lTensor_surjective _ (Submodule.mkQ_surjective _)
136	  exact LinearEquiv.finrank_eq
137	    (((Submodule.quotEquivOfEq _ _ hker.symm).trans
138	      (((LinearMap.range k).mkQ.baseChange t.asIdeal.ResidueField).quotKerEquivOfSurjective
139	        hsurj)).symm)
140	
141	/-- **The pointwise rank-nullity identity** for a two-term complex
142	`k : K → Aⁿ`, at a prime `t`:
143	
144	```
145	dim ker (k ⊗ κ(t))  +  n  =  fiberRank K  +  fiberRank (coker k).
146	```
147	
148	Both fibres are finite-dimensional automatically (`K` is `Module.Finite`, and
149	`κ(t) ⊗ Aⁿ` is `n`-dimensional), so no `finrank` here is a junk `0` — see the
150	module docstring on obligation (b). -/
151	theorem finrank_ker_baseChange_add_eq (n : ℕ) (k : K →ₗ[A] (Fin n → A))
152	    [Module.Finite A K] (t : PrimeSpectrum A) :
153	    Module.finrank t.asIdeal.ResidueField
154	        (LinearMap.ker (k.baseChange t.asIdeal.ResidueField)) + n
155	      = t.asIdeal.fiberRank K
156	        + t.asIdeal.fiberRank ((Fin n → A) ⧸ LinearMap.range k) := by
157	  have h1 : finrank t.asIdeal.ResidueField
158	        (LinearMap.range (k.baseChange t.asIdeal.ResidueField))
159	      + finrank t.asIdeal.ResidueField
160	        (LinearMap.ker (k.baseChange t.asIdeal.ResidueField))
161	      = finrank t.asIdeal.ResidueField (t.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[A] K) :=
162	    (k.baseChange t.asIdeal.ResidueField).finrank_range_add_finrank_ker
163	  have h2 : finrank t.asIdeal.ResidueField
164	        ((t.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[A] (Fin n → A)) ⧸
165	          LinearMap.range (k.baseChange t.asIdeal.ResidueField))
166	      + finrank t.asIdeal.ResidueField
167	        (LinearMap.range (k.baseChange t.asIdeal.ResidueField))
168	      = finrank t.asIdeal.ResidueField (t.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[A] (Fin n → A)) :=
169	    Submodule.finrank_quotient_add_finrank _
170	  have h3 : finrank t.asIdeal.ResidueField
171	      (t.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[A] (Fin n → A)) = n := by
172	    rw [LinearEquiv.finrank_eq (TensorProduct.piScalarRight A t.asIdeal.ResidueField
173	      t.asIdeal.ResidueField (Fin n))]
174	    simp
175	  have h4 : t.asIdeal.fiberRank K
176	      = finrank t.asIdeal.ResidueField (t.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[A] K) := rfl
177	  have h5 := fiberRank_quotRange_eq_finrank_quot_baseChange k t
178	  rw [h4, h5]
179	  omega
180	
181	/-- **The cokernel of a two-term complex is finitely presented**, when the
182	degree-0 term is finite: `Aⁿ` is finitely presented and `range k` is finitely
183	generated. -/
184	instance finitePresentation_quotRange (n : ℕ) (k : K →ₗ[A] (Fin n → A))
185	    [Module.Finite A K] :
186	    Module.FinitePresentation A ((Fin n → A) ⧸ LinearMap.range k) := by
187	  apply Module.finitePresentation_of_surjective (Submodule.mkQ (LinearMap.range k))
188	    (Submodule.mkQ_surjective _)
189	  rw [Submodule.ker_mkQ]
190	  exact Submodule.FG.of_finite
191	
192	/-- **B5's engine: `dim H⁰` of a two-term complex is upper semicontinuous.**
193	
194	For `k : K → Aⁿ` with `K` finitely presented and projective — the shape of
195	`TwoTermFiniteReplacement` — the locus where the fibrewise kernel has dimension
196	at most `e` is open in `Spec A`.
197	
198	No noetherian hypothesis on `A`, no `h¹`-vanishing, and no appeal to
199	`rank_pushforward_eq_fiberH0` (whose `hproj` would force local constancy and
200	so cannot serve semicontinuity — I-0884).
201	
202	Proof: rank-nullity splits `dim ker` into a locally constant part
203	(`fiberRank K`, by `Module.isLocallyConstant_rankAtStalk` — `K` projective is
204	flat) and an upper-semicontinuous part (`fiberRank (coker k)`, by
205	`Ideal.isOpen_fiberRank_le`).  Near any `t₀` where `fiberRank K = r`, the
206	sublevel locus is the intersection of `{fiberRank K = r}` with
207	`{fiberRank (coker k) ≤ e + n − r}`. -/
208	theorem isOpen_finrank_ker_baseChange_le (n : ℕ) (k : K →ₗ[A] (Fin n → A))
209	    [Module.FinitePresentation A K] [Module.Projective A K] (e : ℕ) :
210	    IsOpen {t : PrimeSpectrum A | Module.finrank t.asIdeal.ResidueField
211	      (LinearMap.ker (k.baseChange t.asIdeal.ResidueField)) ≤ e} := by
212	  haveI : Module.Flat A K := Module.Flat.of_projective
213	  have hlc : IsLocallyConstant (fun t : PrimeSpectrum A => t.asIdeal.fiberRank K) := by
214	    have h : (fun t : PrimeSpectrum A => t.asIdeal.fiberRank K)
215	        = Module.rankAtStalk (R := A) K := by
216	      funext t
217	      exact (Module.rankAtStalk_eq (M := K) t).symm
218	    rw [h]
219	    exact Module.isLocallyConstant_rankAtStalk
220	  rw [isOpen_iff_forall_mem_open]
221	  intro t₀ ht₀
222	  set r := t₀.asIdeal.fiberRank K with hr
223	  simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq] at ht₀
224	  have hre : r ≤ e + n := by
225	    have h := finrank_ker_baseChange_add_eq n k t₀
226	    omega
227	  refine ⟨_, ?_, (hlc.isOpen_fiber r).inter
228	    (Ideal.isOpen_fiberRank_le (M := (Fin n → A) ⧸ LinearMap.range k) (e + n - r)),
229	    ⟨rfl, ?_⟩⟩
230	  · rintro t ⟨hV, hW⟩
231	    have h := finrank_ker_baseChange_add_eq n k t
232	    simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq] at hV hW ⊢
233	    rw [hV] at h
234	    omega
235	  · have h := finrank_ker_baseChange_add_eq n k t₀
236	    simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq]
237	    omega
238	
239	/-- **Closed form**: the superlevel locus of the fibrewise kernel dimension is
240	closed.  The complement of `isOpen_finrank_ker_baseChange_le`; this is the
241	direction milestone B6 consumes. -/
242	theorem isClosed_le_finrank_ker_baseChange (n : ℕ) (k : K →ₗ[A] (Fin n → A))
243	    [Module.FinitePresentation A K] [Module.Projective A K] (e : ℕ) :
244	    IsClosed {t : PrimeSpectrum A | e + 1 ≤ Module.finrank t.asIdeal.ResidueField
245	      (LinearMap.ker (k.baseChange t.asIdeal.ResidueField))} := by
246	  have hcompl : {t : PrimeSpectrum A | e + 1 ≤ Module.finrank t.asIdeal.ResidueField
247	        (LinearMap.ker (k.baseChange t.asIdeal.ResidueField))}
248	      = {t : PrimeSpectrum A | Module.finrank t.asIdeal.ResidueField
249	        (LinearMap.ker (k.baseChange t.asIdeal.ResidueField)) ≤ e}ᶜ := by
250	    ext t
251	    simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq, Set.mem_compl_iff, not_le]
252	    omega
253	  rw [hcompl]
254	  exact (isOpen_finrank_ker_baseChange_le n k e).isClosed_compl
255	
256	end TwoTerm
257

8	/-!
9	# The fibre `h⁰` is the fibrewise Čech kernel — with no base-change hypothesis
10	
11	**A repricing, and it corrects obligation (a) of the three recorded at
12	`Picard/FiberH0Comparison.lean`:79-82.**
13	
14	`fiberRank_gammaTop_eq_fiberH0` (same file) proves
15	
16	```
17	dim_κ(t) (κ(t)-fibre of Γ(p_* M, ⊤))  =  p.fiberH0 M t
18	```
19	
20	assuming `hbc`: bijectivity of `TwoTerm.kerBaseChange` over **every** algebra.
21	That hypothesis was recorded as the honest half of cohomology-and-base-change,
22	not free, with a counterexample showing it fails without surjectivity of the
23	differential (`A = ℤ`, `d = ·2`, `B = ℤ/2`).  All of that is correct.
24	
25	What was **not** noticed: `hbc` is consumed in exactly one place, *step 3*, whose
26	only job is to move from `κ(t) ⊗ ker d` to `ker (d ⊗ κ(t))` — i.e. to reach the
27	pushforward's *own* section module.  Steps 4, 5 and 6 alone already prove
28	
29	```
30	dim_κ(t) ker (d ⊗ κ(t))  =  p.fiberH0 M t
31	```
32	
33	with **no `hbc`, no `hfin`, no `hproj`, and no `h¹`-vanishing** — where `d` is
34	the Čech difference map `𝒰.moduleSectionDiffBase p M`.  That is the statement
35	below, and it is the one a semicontinuity argument wants: the *left* side is a
36	kernel of a base-changed map, which is what an upper-semicontinuity engine can
37	say something about, whereas `Γ(p_* M, ⊤)`'s fibre is not.
38	
39	So the pricing was right about `hbc` and wrong about who needs it.  `hbc` is
40	needed to identify the fibre of the **pushforward's sections**; it is not needed
41	to identify the fibre `h⁰`.  A lane routing semicontinuity through the fibrewise
42	Čech kernel does not owe it at all.
43	
44	## What this composes with, and what remains
45	
46	`AlgebraicJacobian.TwoTerm.isOpen_finrank_ker_baseChange_le`
47	(`Picard/TwoTermKernelSemicontinuity.lean`) proves openness of
48	`{t | dim ker (k ⊗ κ(t)) ≤ e}` for `k : K → Aⁿ` with `K` finitely presented
49	projective.  This file's theorem rewrites `p.fiberH0 M t` as exactly such a
50	kernel dimension.  Composing them needs two things that are **still open** and
51	are not supplied here:
52	
53	* the Čech difference map `𝒰.moduleSectionDiffBase p M` must be *replaced* by
54	  one of the engine's shape (`K` projective, target `Aⁿ` free).
55	  `exists_twoTermFiniteReplacement` (`Picard/TwoTermFiniteFree.lean`:545)
56	  produces that shape from noetherian + flat terms + f.g. cohomology, but its
57	  `h0_bijective` field compares the replacement's `H⁰` with the original's over
58	  every algebra, and *that* comparison — not `hbc` — is the remaining
59	  cohomology-and-base-change content;
60	* a **carrier transport**: the engine quantifies over `t : PrimeSpectrum A` for
61	  a bare ring `A`, this theorem over `t : PrimeSpectrum R` with coefficient ring
62	  `Γ(Spec R, ⊤)`.  `Scheme.ΓSpecIso R` is an isomorphism, not an equality, so
63	  the transport is real work of the kind steps 2 and 6 perform by hand — the
64	  obligation (c) already on record.
65	
66	Neither is discharged below.  What is discharged is that `hbc` is not part of
67	either.
68	
69	## References
70	
71	Stacks 02KG (cohomology and base change at `i = 0`), 00NX; Mumford, *Abelian
72	Varieties*, II §5; Hartshorne III 12.8.
73	-/

83	variable {R : CommRingCat.{u}} {X : Scheme.{u}}
84	
85	/-- **The fibre `h⁰` is the dimension of the base-changed Čech kernel**, with no
86	hypotheses beyond the geometric ones.
87	
88	For quasi-compact quasi-separated `p : X ⟶ Spec R`, quasi-coherent `M` with a
89	two-chart affine cover `𝒰`, and `t : Spec R` with affine fibre inclusion:
90	
91	```
92	dim_κ(t) ker (𝒰.moduleSectionDiffBase p M ⊗ κ(t))  =  p.fiberH0 M t.
93	```
94	
95	This is steps 4-6 of `rank_pushforward_eq_fiberH0` in isolation.  Compare
96	`fiberRank_gammaTop_eq_fiberH0`, which reaches the fibre of `Γ(p_* M, ⊤)`
97	instead and needs `hbc` to do so: `hbc` is consumed only in the step that
98	crosses from `ker (d ⊗ κ(t))` to `κ(t) ⊗ ker d`, which this statement never
99	performs.  See the module docstring — this corrects the pricing of obligation
100	(a), it does not close it. -/
101	theorem finrank_ker_moduleSectionDiffBase_baseChange_eq_fiberH0
102	    (p : X ⟶ Spec R) (𝒰 : X.AffineCoverMVSquare) (M : X.Modules)
103	    [M.IsQuasicoherent] [QuasiCompact p] [QuasiSeparated p]
104	    (t : PrimeSpectrum R) [IsAffineHom (p.fiberι t)] :
105	    letI : Algebra Γ(Spec R, ⊤) Γ(Spec ((Spec R).residueField t), ⊤) :=
106	      (((Spec R).fromSpecResidueField t).appLE ⊤ ⊤ le_top).hom.toAlgebra
107	    letI := p.baseSectionsModule M 𝒰.U₁
108	    letI := p.baseSectionsModule M 𝒰.U₂
109	    letI := p.baseSectionsModule M (𝒰.U₁ ⊓ 𝒰.U₂)
110	    Module.finrank Γ(Spec ((Spec R).residueField t), ⊤)
111	        (LinearMap.ker ((𝒰.moduleSectionDiffBase p M).baseChange
112	          Γ(Spec ((Spec R).residueField t), ⊤)))
113	      = p.fiberH0 M t := by
114	  letI aRK : Algebra Γ(Spec R, ⊤) Γ(Spec ((Spec R).residueField t), ⊤) :=
115	    (((Spec R).fromSpecResidueField t).appLE ⊤ ⊤ le_top).hom.toAlgebra
116	  letI m1 := p.baseSectionsModule M 𝒰.U₁
117	  letI m2 := p.baseSectionsModule M 𝒰.U₂
118	  letI m0 := p.baseSectionsModule M (𝒰.U₁ ⊓ 𝒰.U₂)
119	  letI n1 := (p.fiberToSpecResidueField t).baseSectionsModule (p.fiberModule t M)
120	    ((𝒰.preimage (p.fiberι t)).U₁)
121	  letI n2 := (p.fiberToSpecResidueField t).baseSectionsModule (p.fiberModule t M)
122	    ((𝒰.preimage (p.fiberι t)).U₂)
123	  letI n0 := (p.fiberToSpecResidueField t).baseSectionsModule (p.fiberModule t M)
124	    ((𝒰.preimage (p.fiberι t)).U₁ ⊓ (𝒰.preimage (p.fiberι t)).U₂)
125	  letI nT := (p.fiberToSpecResidueField t).baseSectionsModule (p.fiberModule t M)
126	    (⊤ : (p.fiber t).Opens)
127	  -- STEP 4: the fibrewise Čech square (Stacks 02KG at `i = 0`, chart form).
128	  have step4 := finrank_ker_baseChange_residueField 𝒰 p M t
129	  -- STEP 5: the fibre's Čech kernel is its global sections.
130	  have step5 : Module.finrank Γ(Spec ((Spec R).residueField t), ⊤)
131	        (LinearMap.ker ((𝒰.preimage (p.fiberι t)).moduleSectionDiffBase
132	          (p.fiberToSpecResidueField t) (p.fiberModule t M)))
133	      = Module.finrank Γ(Spec ((Spec R).residueField t), ⊤)
134	          Γ(p.fiberModule t M, (⊤ : (p.fiber t).Opens)) :=
135	    (LinearEquiv.finrank_eq ((𝒰.preimage (p.fiberι t)).globalSectionsEquivKerModuleSectionDiffBase
136	      (p.fiberToSpecResidueField t) (p.fiberModule t M))).symm
137	  -- STEP 6: the semilinear transport onto `fiberH0`'s own coefficient field.
138	  have step6 : Module.finrank Γ(Spec ((Spec R).residueField t), ⊤)
139	        Γ(p.fiberModule t M, (⊤ : (p.fiber t).Opens))
140	      = p.fiberH0 M t := by
141	    letI := p.fiberSectionsModule t (p.fiberModule t M)
142	    refine finrank_eq_of_ringEquiv_addEquiv
143	      (Scheme.ΓSpecIso ((Spec R).residueField t)).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv
144	      (AddEquiv.refl _) ?_
145	    intro r m
146	    change r • m = _
147	    rw [Scheme.Hom.baseSectionsModule_smul_def]
148	    change _ = ((p.fiberResidueMap t).hom
149	      ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso ((Spec R).residueField t)).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv r)) • m
150	    congr 1
151	    simp only [Scheme.Hom.fiberResidueMap, CommRingCat.hom_comp, RingHom.comp_apply]
152	    have hLE : (p.fiberToSpecResidueField t).appLE ⊤ ⊤ le_top
153	        = (p.fiberToSpecResidueField t).appTop := Scheme.Hom.appLE_eq_app _
154	    rw [hLE]
155	    congr 1
156	    have h1 := congrArg (fun φ : Γ(Spec ((Spec R).residueField t), ⊤) ⟶
157	        Γ(Spec ((Spec R).residueField t), ⊤) => φ.hom r)
158	      (Scheme.ΓSpecIso ((Spec R).residueField t)).hom_inv_id
159	    simp only [CommRingCat.hom_comp, RingHom.comp_apply, CommRingCat.hom_id,
160	      RingHom.id_apply] at h1
161	    exact h1.symm
162	  rw [step4, step5, step6]
163	
164	end AlgebraicGeometry

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.RigidPushforwardRank

8	/-!
9	# The fibre `h⁰` comparison, without projectivity
10	
11	**The bridge B5 needs, and the one `rank_pushforward_eq_fiberH0` cannot give.**
12	
13	`AlgebraicGeometry.rank_pushforward_eq_fiberH0` (`Picard/RigidPushforwardRank.lean`)
14	proves `sectionsRankAtStalk (p_* M) t = p.fiberH0 M t` under three hypotheses
15	`hfin`, `hproj`, `hbc`.  Its own module docstring establishes that `hproj`
16	(`Module.Projective` of the Čech `H⁰`) is **load-bearing**: dropped, the
17	statement is false, with the counterexample `A = k[x]`,
18	`M = 𝒪_{ℙ¹_A}/x` recorded at `Picard/RigidPushforwardP1Sheaf.lean`:567-576.
19	
20	That is true of *that* statement, and it has been read as a bound on what the
21	machinery can deliver.  It is not.  Reading which step consumes which
22	hypothesis shows `hfin` and `hproj` are used **only in step 1**, the appeal to
23	`Module.rankAtStalk_eq` that converts `sectionsRankAtStalk` — a
24	`Module.rankAtStalk`, which is a statement about the module being flat — into a
25	fibre dimension.  Steps 2 through 6, the entire semilinear transport
26	
27	```
28	κ(t)-fibre of Γ(p_* M, ⊤)  ≅  κ(t) ⊗ ker d  ≅  ker (d ⊗ κ(t))
29	                           ≅  ker d_t       ≅  Γ(X_t, M_t)
30	```
31	
32	consume **neither `hfin` nor `hproj`** — verified by a fresh-context review,
33	which reproduced the original from this theorem by adding only
34	`Module.rankAtStalk_eq`.  So this file states the comparison with those two
35	hypotheses removed:
36	
37	* `fiberRank_gammaTop_eq_fiberH0` — no `hfin`, no `hproj`, only `hbc`.
38	
39	**But dropping `hfin` has a cost, and it must be stated here rather than
40	discovered later.**  The original's docstring
41	(`Picard/RigidPushforwardRank.lean`:138-145) closes a junk-value hazard:
42	`Module.finrank` returns `0` in the infinite-dimensional case, on *both* sides,
43	so the identity could hold vacuously as `0 = 0`.  Its argument that this cannot
44	happen runs entirely through `hfin` (`ker d` finite ⟹ `κ(t) ⊗ ker d` is
45	finite-dimensional ⟹ steps 3-6 carry that to `Γ(X_t, M_t)`).  `hbc` does **not**
46	replace it: taking `d = 0 : M₀ →ₗ[A] PUnit` makes `hbc` hold for every `B`
47	(trivially surjective) with `ker d = M₀` arbitrary, so an infinite-dimensional
48	`ker d` is compatible with `hbc` and both sides then read `0`.
49	
50	So the theorem below is honest but weaker than the original in a way the
51	hypothesis list alone does not show: **it is informative only where `ker d` is
52	finite-dimensional over `κ(t)`**, and it does not certify that itself.  A
53	consumer wanting a non-vacuous reading must supply finite-dimensionality
54	separately — which is *not* the same as supplying `hfin` (`Module.Finite` over
55	the base), and is the reason the statement is still worth having.
56	
57	## What this buys for B5, and the obligation it does NOT remove
58	
59	`Scheme.HasH0Semicontinuity` (`Picard/SemicontinuityH0.lean`) asks for openness
60	of `{t | q.fiberH0 L t ≤ n}`.  The `sectionsRankAtStalk` form cannot be an input
61	to it: semicontinuity is only informative where the fibre dimension *jumps*, and
62	`hproj` forces it locally constant (`Module.isLocallyConstant_rankAtStalk`).
63	The `Ideal.fiberRank` form here has no such effect, which is the point of the
64	restatement.
65	
66	**It does not, however, already match
67	`Scheme.Modules.isOpen_pointRank_le`** (`Picard/PointRankSemicontinuity.lean`),
68	and an earlier revision of this docstring claimed it did.  Measured: the two are
69	*not the same term* and `rfl` between them fails.  `pointRank` unfolds (through
70	`pointRank_eq_chartFiberRank` at `V = ⊤`) to a `fiberRank` taken at a prime of
71	`Γ(Spec R, ⊤)` with the `Γ(Spec R, ⊤)`-module structure, whereas the conclusion
72	below uses `t.asIdeal` for `t : PrimeSpectrum R` with the `R`-module structure.
73	Bridging them needs a `ΓSpecIso` transport of exactly the kind steps 2 and 6
74	perform by hand, and the only in-tree lemma relating the two worlds,
75	`Scheme.Modules.rankAtStalk_sections_eq_pointRank`
76	(`Picard/FlatteningStratificationUniversal.lean`:204), carries
77	`[Module.Flat]` + `[Module.Finite]` binders — i.e. precisely what was dropped.
78	
79	So B5 has **three** open obligations, not one: (a) `hbc` without
80	`h¹`-vanishing, (b) finite-dimensionality to defeat the junk-value reading, and
81	(c) this carrier bridge between `pointRank` and `Ideal.fiberRank`.  (c) was
82	unlisted until a fresh-context review found it.
83	
84	**CORRECTED, and both corrections are against this list, not against the Lean
85	below.** Two of those three have since been repriced or closed:
86	
87	* **(b) is CLOSED** — `Picard/TwoTermKernelSemicontinuity.lean`.  Stated on a
88	  two-term complex `k : K → Aⁿ` with `K` merely `Module.Finite`,
89	  finite-dimensionality of both fibres is *synthesised*, not supplied: it is a
90	  consequence of the shape, so no hypothesis defeats the junk-value reading —
91	  there is nothing to defeat.
92	* **(a) was MISPRICED, and the misprice is mine.**  The counterexample below is
93	  correct and `hbc` really is not free.  But `hbc` is consumed in **step 3
94	  only**, whose job is to cross from `ker (d ⊗ κ(t))` to `κ(t) ⊗ ker d` — that
95	  is, to reach *this* theorem's conclusion about `Γ(p_* M, ⊤)`.  Steps 4-6 alone
96	  already give `dim ker (d ⊗ κ(t)) = p.fiberH0 M t`, with no `hbc` at all;
97	  that is `finrank_ker_moduleSectionDiffBase_baseChange_eq_fiberH0`
98	  (`Picard/FiberH0CechKernel.lean`).  So `hbc` identifies the fibre of the
99	  *pushforward's section module*; it does **not** identify the fibre `h⁰`, and a
100	  route through the fibrewise Čech kernel does not owe it.
101	
102	(c) stands, unchanged.  What replaces (a) is a different obligation: the Čech
103	difference map must be *replaced* by a complex of the engine's shape, and
104	`TwoTermFiniteReplacement.h0_bijective` — not `kerBaseChange` — is where the
105	residual cohomology-and-base-change content sits.
106	
107	## What is still open
108	
109	The remaining hypothesis `hbc` — bijectivity of
110	`AlgebraicJacobian.TwoTerm.kerBaseChange` over every algebra — is *not* free,
111	and it is worth being precise about why, because the temptation is to hope it
112	falls out of flatness.
113	
114	Its only producer in the tree,
115	`TwoTerm.bijective_kerBaseChange_of_surjective`, needs `d` **surjective** —
116	i.e. `h¹`-vanishing.  Surjectivity is genuinely necessary and not an artefact
117	of that proof: take `A = ℤ`, `d = (2 · ·) : ℤ → ℤ`, which is injective with
118	both terms flat but not surjective.  Then `ker d = 0`, so `B ⊗ ker d = 0` for
119	every `B`, while over `B = ℤ/2` the base-changed map is zero and
120	`ker (d ⊗ B) = ℤ/2 ≠ 0`.  So `kerBaseChange` is not bijective, with flatness
121	of both terms intact.
122	
123	What this file therefore does is **relocate** part of the B5 obligation, not
124	discharge it.  It converts "find a projectivity-free rank bridge" — impossible,
125	and the route the gate's own docstring prescribes — into the three named items
126	(a), (b), (c) above, of which (a) is the honest half of
127	cohomology-and-base-change (Stacks 02KG).  Correctly located; all three open.
128	
129	One route not yet followed: a `TwoTermFiniteReplacement` supplies
130	`h0_bijective` for *every* algebra `B` with **no** surjectivity hypothesis
131	(it is a field of the structure, and `exists_twoTermFiniteReplacement` needs
132	only noetherian + flat + f.g. cohomology).  That is a comparison between the
133	`H⁰`s of the replacement and original complexes rather than the
134	`kerBaseChange` of one map, so it does not immediately give `hbc`; whether it
135	can be made to is the next thing to try.
136	
137	## References
138	
139	Stacks 02KG (cohomology and base change at `i = 0`), 00NX; Mumford,
140	*Abelian Varieties*, II §5; Hartshorne III 12.8, 12.11.
141	-/
142	
143	set_option autoImplicit false
144	
145	universe u
146	
147	open CategoryTheory AlgebraicGeometry Module Limits TensorProduct
148	
149	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
150	
151	variable {R : CommRingCat.{u}} {X : Scheme.{u}}
152	
153	/-- **The fibre-`h⁰` comparison, with no projectivity and no finiteness.**
154	
155	For quasi-compact quasi-separated `p : X ⟶ Spec R`, quasi-coherent `M` carrying
156	a two-chart affine cover `𝒰`, and `t : Spec R` with affine fibre inclusion, the
157	`κ(t)`-fibre dimension of the base section module `Γ(p_* M, ⊤)` equals the
158	fibre `h⁰`, assuming only the base-change bijectivity `hbc`.
159	
160	This is steps 2-6 of `rank_pushforward_eq_fiberH0` with step 1 — the only step
161	that consumes `hfin`/`hproj` — removed, and the conclusion restated on
162	`Ideal.fiberRank` rather than on `sectionsRankAtStalk`.  See the module
163	docstring for why that restatement is what milestone B5 needs. -/
164	theorem fiberRank_gammaTop_eq_fiberH0
165	    (p : X ⟶ Spec R) (𝒰 : X.AffineCoverMVSquare) (M : X.Modules)
166	    [M.IsQuasicoherent] [QuasiCompact p] [QuasiSeparated p]
167	    (t : PrimeSpectrum R) [IsAffineHom (p.fiberι t)]
168	    (hbc :
169	      letI := p.baseSectionsModule M 𝒰.U₁
170	      letI := p.baseSectionsModule M 𝒰.U₂
171	      letI := p.baseSectionsModule M (𝒰.U₁ ⊓ 𝒰.U₂)
172	      ∀ (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra Γ(Spec R, ⊤) B],
173	        Function.Bijective (AlgebraicJacobian.TwoTerm.kerBaseChange
174	          (𝒰.moduleSectionDiffBase p M) B)) :
175	    Module.finrank t.asIdeal.ResidueField
176	        (t.asIdeal.Fiber Γ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward p).obj M, (⊤ : (Spec R).Opens)))
177	      = p.fiberH0 M t := by
178	  letI m1 := p.baseSectionsModule M 𝒰.U₁
